business_problem: Changan needed a high-performance AI computing center that could support smart-driving, connected-car and large-model R&D at much larger scale than its existing fragmented resources allowed.
solution_summary: Changan Automobile and Baidu AI Cloud built an AI computing center that acts as the technical base for the automaker's large-model, intelligent-driving and connected-car programs. Baidu's BaiGe heterogeneous-compute platform provides the foundation, while Changan's 'Xinghuan' platform sits on top to coordinate data collection, processing, labeling, training, evaluation and deployment across multiple clusters. The design is more than a raw GPU farm: it unifies scheduling for compute and storage resources, carries model-training optimization for Changan's own industry models, and supports additional business systems such as smart assistants, connected-car data analysis and new-energy supervision reporting. That turns the computing center into an enterprise AI operating platform rather than a single research cluster. By linking training infrastructure, labeled data accumulation and application deployment in one stack, Changan can keep new-model development, assistant features and automotive AI services on a common managed backbone.

data_flow: Automotive data is collected, processed and labeled through Xinghuan, trained on BaiGe-backed compute resources, then evaluated and deployed into smart-driving, vehicle-assistant and enterprise AI applications.
business_outcome: Changan gained a unified AI infrastructure base that accelerates model R&D, raises GPU efficiency and supports broader enterprise and in-vehicle AI adoption.
